references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew's version of Jesus' eschatological discourse: 'Truly, I tell you, this generation will not pass away before all these things take place' ([ref:Matt 24:34|Matthew 24:34]). An identical statement in the same context.

Parallel passage in Mark's version of the Olivet Discourse: 'Truly, I tell you, this generation will not pass away before all these things take place' ([ref:Mark 13:30|Mark 13:30]). The same promise from Jesus is recorded in all three Synoptic Gospels.

Jesus says that 'all these things will come upon this generation' ([ref:Matt 23:36|Matthew 23:36]), referring to the judgment that will fall on the generation that rejected him. The same use of 'this generation' (ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη) as in Luke 21:32.

Jesus says that some of those standing there will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom ([ref:Matt 16:28|Matthew 16:28]). A similar timeframe where fulfillment is linked to the living generation.

Jesus says that some of those standing there will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God come with power ([ref:Mark 9:1|Mark 9:1]). A parallel statement indicating that fulfillment will occur within the lifetime of the current generation.

The immediately following verse emphasizes the certainty of these words: 'Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away' ([ref:Luk 21:33|Luke 21:33]). This confirms the absolute reliability of the promise given in verse 32.

Jesus says that the blood of all the prophets will be required from 'this generation' ([ref:Luk 11:51|Luke 11:51]). The same expression 'this generation' is used for the generation living at the time of Jesus who will experience God's judgment.

Psalm 95 is quoted regarding the generation that provoked God's anger in the wilderness: 'Therefore I was angry with this generation' ([ref:Hebr 3:10|Hebrews 3:10]). The term 'generation' (γενεά) is used for a group of people under God's judgment, in a similar way as in Luke 21:32.

Jesus says that some of those standing there will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God ([ref:Luk 9:27|Luke 9:27]). Luke's own parallel to the promise that certain things will happen within the time of the living generation.
